english.title: Cause serious injury by driving whilst disqualified
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) caused serious injury to **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) by driving a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..), and, at that time, you were committing an offence under section 103(1)(b) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 by driving when you were disqualified from holding or obtaining a driving licence to drive a motor vehicle of that class
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3ZD of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

english.notes:
Serious injury means -
(a) in England and Wales, physical harm which amounts to grievous bodily harm for the purposes of the Offences against the Person Act 1861, and (b) in Scotland, severe physical injury.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: 4 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Obligatory disqualification and endorsement.

Obligatory endorsement - licence endorsed three to eleven penalty points.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

For offences committed on or after 12th March 2015 the fine on summary conviction is unlimited, see section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
